texts.li: {A_nameDef} came to the council with a request {A_pronoun} had clearly rehearsed. More than anything, {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and between the hauling, the cleaning and every other chore on the roster, there's no time left for it.\n\n{A_nameDef} is asking to be let off the dull work for a season. Others would have to pick it up, and they're listening closely.

Every evening {A_nameDef} comes in from the day's chores too tired to do anything but sleep. {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and at this rate it will never happen.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council for lighter duties for a while, to make some real progress. The roster is already tight, and the people who would take up the slack aren't pleased.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} off the chores for a season
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is off the chore roster for now and puts every spare hour into the dream. The others are doing more of the hauling, and some of them resent it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} got the season off and spent the first week of it mostly asleep, while the others covered {A_possessive} chores.

li.label: One free afternoon in three
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gets every third afternoon off the roster. It's less than {A_pronoun} asked for, but it's a start, and the others hardly notice the difference.

li.label: The chores come first
li.outcome: The roster stays as it is. {A_nameDef} went back to hauling, and the dream will have to wait.
li.riskOutcome: The roster stays as it is. {A_nameDef} said nothing, and has done every chore at half speed since.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has a plan to {GOAL}, written down this time, with figures. The figures add up to 150 silver from the colony's purse, for tools, books and whatever a passing trader can supply.\n\n{A_nameDef} swears every coin will go toward the dream. The purse has never been heavy, and the others know it.

A trader passed through last week, and {A_nameDef} spent the whole visit at the wagons asking questions. {A_nameDef} is now sure that with the right supplies, {A_pronoun} could finally {GOAL}.\n\nThe supplies cost 150 silver. {A_nameDef} has none, and is asking the council for it.

li.label: Give {A_nameDef} 150 silver
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} got the silver and spent it carefully, accounting for every coin. {A_nameDef} is sure it was worth it; some of the others think it was wasted.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} took the 150 silver to the next trader and came back with a crate that turned out to be mostly packing straw. {A_nameDef} is mortified, and the silver is gone.

li.label: Give 50 silver
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} got fifty silver, a third of what the plan called for, and has already started reworking the figures.

li.label: Not from the colony's purse
li.outcome: The silver stays in the purse. {A_nameDef} folded the plan up small and put it away in a drawer.

li.label: Give the silver, and send our best haggler along
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} went with {A_nameDef} to the next trader and talked the price down to 120 silver. {A_nameDef} came back with everything on the list and a little respect for haggling.

outcomes.li: [b:past:trader] {B_nameDef} has bought and sold for a living and knew every trick the trader tried. {A_nameDef} got everything on the list for 120 silver.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} haggled hard and got the price down to 120 silver, and neither of them looked under the top layer of the crate. It was mostly straw.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and has decided that the person to help is {B_nameDef}, who has seen more of the world than most and knows how things get done.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants {B_nameDef}'s evenings, every one of them, for the next season. {B_nameDef} hasn't been asked yet, and would like to be.

For days {A_nameDef} has followed {B_nameDef} around with questions about work, about life, and about how a person sets out to {GOAL}. {B_nameDef} has answered some of them and hidden from the rest.\n\nNow {A_nameDef} wants the council to make {B_nameDef} a mentor, with time set aside for it. {B_nameDef} isn't sure about that.

li.label: Ask {B_nameDef} to make the time
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} now spends the evenings with {A_nameDef}, talking through every step of the plan. {B_nameDef} grumbled at first, but has come to enjoy it.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} gave {A_nameDef} two evenings and spent most of them explaining why the plan was wrong. The second ended in a shouting match, and they've avoided each other since.

li.label: Free up {B_nameDef}'s evenings
li.outcome: Some of {B_nameDef}'s chores were shared out among the others, leaving {B_nameDef}'s evenings free for teaching. {A_nameDef} is delighted and {B_nameDef} is flattered. The others have more hauling to do.

li.label: That's between the two of them
li.outcome: The council left it to {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef}. {A_nameDef} still asks questions, and {B_nameDef} still avoids some of them.

texts.li: At dinner, {B_nameDef} told the whole table that {A_nameDef}'s wish to {GOAL} is a waste of everyone's time and food. A few people laughed, but {A_nameDef} didn't.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants the council to say in public that it's a fine thing to want. {B_nameDef} wants the council to agree that it's foolish.

{B_nameDef} has taken to calling {A_nameDef} "the dreamer," and not kindly. {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and {B_nameDef} thinks it's foolish and says so whenever {A_nameDef} walks into a room.\n\nIt came to shouting this morning, and both of them have brought it to the council.

li.label: Stand behind {A_nameDef}'s dream
li.outcome: The council said at dinner that a person's dream is their own business and nothing to mock. {A_nameDef} sat up straighter, and {B_nameDef} chewed loudly through the rest of the meal.
li.riskOutcome: The council stood behind {A_nameDef}'s dream, in public. {B_nameDef} took it as a personal insult, and has been telling anyone who'll listen that the council has gone soft.

li.label: Hear {B_nameDef} out
li.outcome: The council let {B_nameDef} make the whole case against the dream. Some of it was fair. {A_nameDef} left before the end.
li.riskOutcome: The council let {B_nameDef} make the whole case against the dream. {A_nameDef} left before the end and wandered off into the wilds alone.

li.label: Settle it with a wager
li.outcome: The council set the terms: if {A_nameDef} pulls it off, {B_nameDef} cooks for a week and apologizes at dinner. {A_nameDef} is working at it harder than ever, and {B_nameDef} is starting to look worried.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: The council stayed out of it. {B_nameDef} took that as permission to keep up the mockery, and {A_nameDef} has stopped mentioning the dream.
li.riskOutcome: The council stayed out of it, so {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} settled it themselves, behind the storeroom, with fists.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}. {B_nameDef} has a dream of {B_possessive} own. Neither is unreasonable, but a colony this size has only so many free hours, so much spare silver and one decent workbench, and each of them wants all of it.\n\nThey've been getting in each other's way for weeks, and now they want the council to say whose dream comes first.

{A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and {B_nameDef} is chasing a different dream entirely. Both need time off the roster and a share of the stores, and the colony can only spare enough for one.\n\nEach of them made a good speech to the council, and each speech ended with the other one waiting.

li.label: {A_nameDef}'s dream comes first
li.outcome: The council put {A_nameDef}'s dream first, and {A_nameDef} got straight to work. {B_nameDef} has been told to wait, and complains about it to anyone who will listen.

li.label: {B_nameDef}'s dream comes first
li.outcome: The council put {B_nameDef} first. {A_nameDef} has been told {A_pronoun} must wait {A_possessive} turn to {GOAL}, and is bitter about it.

li.label: Split everything down the middle
li.outcome: Each of them got half the free hours, half the stores and alternate days at the bench. Neither is satisfied, though the rest of the colony thinks it's fair.

li.label: Make them help each other
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to pool their time and help each other. It was awkward at first, but now they're up late most nights planning both dreams together.
li.riskOutcome: The council told them to help each other. One afternoon at the shared workbench was enough for {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to come to blows.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been restless for weeks. {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and here it seems further away every day. A trader's stories about the settlements to the east did the rest, and now {A_nameDef} wants to leave with the next caravan and see whether life is kinder somewhere else.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked for the council's blessing, though the others suspect {A_pronoun} also hopes to be talked out of it.

A pack has been sitting half full by {A_nameDef}'s bed for days. Late last night {A_nameDef} admitted to thinking about leaving with the next caravan. {A_nameDef} wants to {GOAL}, and no longer believes it can happen here.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to know what the council thinks.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to stay
li.outcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to stay, and promised real help with the dream. {A_nameDef} unpacked the bag that night, slowly, and seemed relieved to have been asked.
li.riskOutcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to stay, and {A_nameDef} agreed, but a few things are still packed in a bag by the door.

li.label: Give {A_nameDef} the council's blessing
li.outcome: The council gave {A_nameDef} its blessing. {A_nameDef} walked to the gate, stood there a long while, and came back in for dinner.

li.label: The colony needs every hand
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} the colony can't spare anyone. {A_nameDef} unpacked the bag without a word and has been staring at the walls ever since.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} decide alone
li.outcome: The decision was left to {A_nameDef}. The caravan came and went, and {A_nameDef} watched it go from the wall. The pack is still by the bed.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been trying to {GOAL} for a long time, and lately has stopped trying. Last night, staring into the fire, {A_nameDef} said maybe it was never going to happen, and it was time to stop pretending.\n\n{A_nameDef}'s friends have asked the council to step in. {A_nameDef} hasn't asked for anything.

This morning {A_nameDef}'s notes turned up on the trash heap, months of plans to {GOAL}, torn neatly in half. {A_nameDef} says it doesn't matter, but has hardly eaten since.\n\nThe council can try to get {A_nameDef} going again, or let {A_objective} set it down in peace.

li.label: Rally the colony behind {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: At dinner the council asked each colonist to give {A_nameDef} one reason not to give up, all the way around the table. {A_nameDef} was up before dawn the next morning, back at work on the dream.
li.riskOutcome: At dinner the council asked each colonist to give {A_nameDef} one reason not to give up. Halfway around the table it began to feel like pity, and {A_nameDef} left before it reached the end.

li.label: A few easy days to think it over
li.outcome: The council gave {A_nameDef} a few days off the roster. {A_nameDef} spent them walking, sleeping and, near the end, sketching something new on the back of an old plan.

li.label: There's no shame in letting it go
li.outcome: The council didn't push. {A_nameDef} was told there's no shame in setting a dream down, nodded, and has stopped talking about it.
li.riskOutcome: The council didn't push. {A_nameDef} nodded, said thank you, and wandered off alone toward the hills.

li.label: Tell {A_nameDef} to toughen up
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} that everyone has bad days and the work still has to be done. {A_nameDef} heard it out and went back to work without a word.
li.riskOutcome: The council told {A_nameDef} to toughen up. Out of spite, {A_nameDef} has spent every spare minute on the dream since.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} came to the council with an odd request. People die out here without warning, {A_nameDef} said, and {A_pronoun} may not live to {GOAL}. If that happens, {A_nameDef} wants the dream written down somewhere, so the colony remembers it and perhaps takes it up.\n\n{B_nameDef}, who was in the room, hasn't said a word since.

Lately {A_nameDef} has been putting things in order, mending old clothes, giving away odds and ends, writing in a journal late into the night. Today {A_nameDef} asked the council for one more thing.\n\nIf death comes before {A_nameDef} can {GOAL}, {A_pronoun} wants the colony to remember that this was the dream, and not leave it forgotten in a drawer. {B_nameDef} has been listening closely, and looks troubled.

li.label: Write it into the colony's records
li.outcome: After dinner the council gathered the colony, read {A_nameDef}'s dream aloud, and wrote it into the records. {A_nameDef} stood at the back with wet eyes.

li.label: {B_nameDef} promises to carry it on
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} stood up and promised that if the worst happens, {B_pronoun} will see the dream through. {A_nameDef} held on to {B_possessive} hand for a long while.

li.label: A private promise from the council
li.outcome: The council promised {A_nameDef}, without any fuss, that the dream would not be forgotten. {A_nameDef} seemed satisfied, and lighter for it.

li.label: Don't talk like that
li.outcome: The council wouldn't discuss it. {A_nameDef} tried twice more at dinner, was told not to be morbid both times, and gave up.
